item.title: CBSA reminds travellers of upcoming closure of the Remote Area Border Crossing Program and expansion of telephone reporting
item.description:
The Canada Border Services Agency said the Remote Area Border Crossing Program is set to shut at 11:59 p.m. on November 30, 2026. After that date, travellers entering Canada at remote locations will need to call in through designated telephone reporting sites. The CBSA said 17 new telephone reporting sites are already operational, and it has identified more locations after consultations with local and Indigenous communities and other interested parties. Details on the additional sites will be added to the CBSA directory as they open.

item.title: East Coast Diesel Stocks Hit Record Low as Trucking Costs Surge
item.description:
East Coast diesel supply is the tightest for this time of year on record, according to Department of Energy data reported by Dosya Haber. Inventories fell below 52 million barrels as of last Friday, compared with the roughly 62 million barrels the region typically holds in May. Pump prices have risen with the drop in stocks. The national average reached a record $5.62 per gallon, and the East Coast averaged $5.90, up 63% since the start of the year. Analysts quoted in the report see few signs of a quick turnaround, and say higher prices may remain the main way to draw more fuel cargoes into the Northeast.

item.title: Hijacked Carrier Credentials Drive Surge in U.S. Cargo Theft Values
CBSA seizes over $25 million in nicotine products across Southern Ontario
item.description:
Canada Border Services Agency officers at land ports of entry across Southern Ontario seized more than $25 million worth of illicit nicotine products over four days in November. The products were in commercial freight coming in from the United States. The agency said the seizures help disrupt organized crime, and the federal government said it is investing $1.3 billion to strengthen border security and the immigration system under its Border Plan.
